title: Final Project: Full Pipeline
concept: Set up a complete XIOM project pipeline — scaffolding, version control, CI/CD, multi-platform builds, cross-compilation, and release automation.
why: Individual tools are useful. Integrated pipelines are essential. This capstone connects everything from L6 into a production-ready development workflow.
theory:
## The Complete Project Setup

### Project Requirements

1. **Scaffold**: `xiom init` for proper project structure
2. **Git**: Initialized with `.gitignore`, branches, tags
3. **CI/CD**: GitHub Actions with format → lint → test → build → verify
4. **Multi-platform**: Build for Linux, macOS, Windows
5. **Cross-compile**: WASM target for web deployment
6. **Release**: Automated versioning, changelog, publishing
7. **Docs**: Auto-generated and published
8. **Badges**: CI status, version, license in README

### Pipeline Stages

```yaml
# Complete CI/CD Pipeline
stages:
  - name: Format Check
    run: xiom fmt --check src/
    on: [push, PR]

  - name: Lint
    run: xiom lint --deny-warnings src/
    on: [push, PR]

  - name: Type Check
    run: xiom check
    on: [push, PR]

  - name: Test
    run: xiom test
    on: [push, PR]

  - name: Verify Contracts
    run: xiom verify src/
    on: [PR]

  - name: Build (All Platforms)
    run: |
      xiom build --release --target x86_64-linux-gnu
      xiom build --release --target x86_64-apple-darwin
      xiom build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
      xiom build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
    on: [main]

  - name: Benchmark
    run: xiom bench
    on: [main]

  - name: Release
    run: |
      xiom pkg publish
      create-github-release
    on: [tag v*]
```

### Complete Project Checklist

```
[ ] xiom init with correct template
[ ] package.xi with complete metadata
[ ] .gitignore with target/, .xiom-cache/
[ ] xiom-toolchain.toml pinned to stable
[ ] xiomfmt.toml configured
[ ] xiomlint.toml configured
[ ] .github/workflows/ci.yml
[ ] README.md with badges
[ ] CHANGELOG.md started
[ ] CONTRIBUTING.md
[ ] All tests passing
[ ] Documentation written
[ ] Multi-platform builds verified
```

tips: A complete pipeline catches issues at the RIGHT time — format issues on save, type errors on check, regressions on test
Start with the minimum pipeline (format + lint + test) and add stages as needed
The pipeline is documentation — it shows exactly what quality gates your code must pass
Automate everything you check manually — if you check it, CI should check it too
common_mistakes: Over-engineering the pipeline early — start simple, add complexity with need
CI that takes 30 minutes — keep the basic pipeline under 5 minutes for fast feedback
Not documenting the pipeline — new team members should understand quality gates from reading CI config
